units.name: Rural Levies
units.description: Farmhands pressed into service with mattocks and hunting spears. They fill a battle line and little else, but every village can raise them.

units.name: Bolt Throwers
units.description: Torsion engines that hurl iron-tipped shafts through shield and man alike. Their crews double as sappers when walls must come down.

units.name: Stone Onagers
units.description: Kicking beasts of timber and sinew that lob quarried stone over any rampart. Slow on the march, terrible once emplaced.

units.name: Coastal Galley
units.description: A light two-banked galley fit for patrol work, escort duty, and ferrying troops along the shore. Every harbor town can lay one down.

units.name: Town Watch
units.description: Townsmen issued a spear, a shield, and a rota of wall duty. They keep order at home and die bravely enough when war finds them there.

units.name: Velites
units.description: Young men in wolfskin caps who open the battle with a hail of javelins, then slip back through the maniples. Poor, quick, and eager to be noticed.

units.name: Hastati
units.description: The first line of the legion: younger citizens with heavy javelin, short sword, and tall shield. They blunt the enemy so older men need not.

units.name: Principes
units.description: Citizens in their prime, mailed and steady, who take the fight where the hastati faltered. The second line is where battles are usually decided.

units.name: Triarii
units.description: Grey-bearded veterans who kneel behind their spears as the last line of the Republic. When matters come to the triarii, matters are grave indeed.

units.name: Equites
units.description: Wealthy young citizens serving on horseback more from duty than aptitude. Adequate for scouting and pursuit; do not ask more of them.

units.name: Cohort Legionaries
units.description: Professional soldiers of the reformed legions, uniformly armed and drilled to march, dig, and kill on command. The state pays them; the state owns them.

units.name: Eagle Cohort
units.description: The senior cohort that marches beside the legion's eagle, filled with decorated veterans of twenty campaigns. Losing the standard is worse than dying.

units.name: Auxilia Spearmen
units.description: Provincial subjects serving under Roman officers for pay and the promise of citizenship. Cheap, plentiful, and steadier than their paymasters admit.

units.name: Auxilia Archers
units.description: Rome breeds few bowmen, so she hires the provinces' best and drills them into ranks. They give the legions the reach nature denied them.

units.name: Legionary Cavalry
units.description: Professional horsemen attached to the reformed legions, better mounted and better paid than the old equites. They guard the flanks and finish the routed.

units.name: Oathsworn of Mars
units.description: Soldiers consecrated at the great altar of Mars, sworn to return with their shields or upon them. They do not break, because the god is watching.

units.name: Praetorian Escort
units.description: Hand-picked horsemen bound to a commander's person and career. Where the general's crest goes, their blades follow.

units.name: Corvus Quinquereme
units.description: A heavy five fitted with a spiked boarding bridge that turns sea fights into land fights. Rome cannot out-sail her rivals, so she out-stabs them.

units.name: Polis Garrison
units.description: Poorer citizens with an old spear and their grandfather's shield, mustered to man the walls. In close ranks they can still make a hedge of points.

units.name: Peltasts
units.description: Javelin men with crescent shields who harry, withdraw, and harry again. Cheap to raise and infuriating to catch.

units.name: Hellenic Archers
units.description: Bowmen trained in the island fashion to arc volleys over the phalanx's sarissas. The pike holds the enemy; the arrow bleeds him.

units.name: Citizen Hoplites
units.description: Free men of the polis in bronze and linen, shoulder to shoulder behind the great round shield. Each protects his neighbor, and so the city stands.

units.name: Chosen Hoplites
units.description: The picked band of the league, drilled year-round at public expense in the old Laconian manner. Their line has never been bought and rarely been bent.

units.name: Levy Pikemen
units.description: Farm boys handed a sixteen-foot sarissa and taught to lower it on command. From the front, indistinguishable from veterans until the line shivers.

units.name: Phalanx Pikemen
units.description: The standing pike blocks of the successor kingdoms, five ranks of iron points presented to the foe. Frontally unapproachable; guard the flanks.

units.name: Silver Pikes
units.description: Veterans of the royal army whose silvered shields mark a lifetime under the sarissa. Kings rise and fall on whether these men hold.

units.name: Hellenic Light Horse
units.description: Javelin-armed riders hired from the horse-breeding borderlands. They screen the phalanx and run down whatever it breaks.

units.name: Companion Lancers
units.description: Noble horsemen in the tradition of the great king's own squadron, striking with the long lance at the hinge of a battle. The hammer to the phalanx's anvil.

units.name: Thracian Falxmen
units.description: Hillmen swinging the two-handed curved blade that shears through shield-rims and helmets. What they lack in armor they repay in ruin.

units.name: Armored Tuskers
units.description: Great eastern elephants plated in bronze, towers swaying with javelin men. Horses bolt and battle lines dissolve at their coming.

units.name: Strategos Guard
units.description: Companions of the commander's own household, armored in the royal style. Their duty is his life; their reward is his memory of it.

units.name: War Trireme
units.description: The classic three-banked ram-ship, rowed by free men who know why they row. Handled well, it guts heavier vessels and is gone before they settle.

units.name: Hill Levies
units.description: Mountain villagers with axes, knives, and hide shields, called down when the satrap demands men. Poor soldiers, but tireless ones.

units.name: Eastern Spearmen
units.description: Wicker-shielded spearmen in the old imperial pattern, raised to hold ground while the horse decides the day. They ask only that the horse hurry.

units.name: Eastern Foot Archers
units.description: Bowmen raised in lands where every boy learns the string before the plow. Massed, their arrow-storms darken the ground they fall on.

units.name: Bronze Shield Pikemen
units.description: The kingdom's Hellenized guard regiments, pike-armed behind burnished bronze faces. Persian blood, Macedonian drill, royal pay.

units.name: Steppe-Bred Horse Archers
units.description: Riders who loose over the shoulder at full gallop and are gone before the shaft lands. Chasing them is how armies die tired.

units.name: Armored Horse Archers
units.description: Retainers of the great houses in scale corselets, shooting from the saddle and closing with the mace when the quivers run dry.

units.name: Cataphracts
units.description: Man and horse sheathed entire in iron scale, a wall that gallops. Their lance-charge is the argument the horse archers were saving.

units.name: Scythed Chariots
units.description: Four-horse cars with whirling blades bolted to the axles, driven flat-out at the enemy's center. Against steady troops a gamble; against shaken ones a massacre.

units.name: Eastern Lancers
units.description: Landed gentry with lance and light armor, the everyday cavalry of the eastern kingdoms. Not the iron fist, but a serviceable open hand.

units.name: Satrap's Chosen
units.description: Armored kinsmen riding at their lord's stirrup, sworn by fire and salt. To outlive him in battle would be a disgrace none intends to suffer.

units.name: Punic Levy Spears
units.description: Subject Libyans mustered under Punic officers to watch walls and caravans. The Republic prefers to spend silver, but sometimes it must spend these.

units.name: Libyan Javelinmen
units.description: Hard-running skirmishers from the African hinterland, casting darts and insults in equal measure. They soften a line the citizen bands will finish.

units.name: Citizen Band
units.description: Merchants' sons in white linen and bronze, fighting in the close Hellenic manner. Carthage arms her own only when the stakes are her own.

units.name: Sacred Band of Baal
units.description: Sons of the noblest houses, dedicated before the fires of Baal Hammon and armored like temple statues. They are buried where they fall, facing the enemy.

units.name: Punic Light Horse
units.description: Riders schooled in the African fashion — no saddle, no rest, no warning. They circle a column for days until it forgets what safety felt like.

units.name: Punic Noble Horse
units.description: The great trading families' own squadrons, superbly mounted and jealous of their honor. Rare enough that generals hoard them like the silver they cost.

units.name: Forest War Elephants
units.description: Smaller beasts taken from the Atlas woods, driven by hired mahouts who ride with a spike for emergencies. What they start, panic finishes.

units.name: Suffet's Guard
units.description: Citizen horsemen of proven family who attend the Republic's commanders abroad. Their loyalty is to Carthage; the general merely carries it.

units.name: Punic Quinquereme
units.description: A five built to numbered patterns in the covered ship-sheds, crewed by rowers who learned the oar in the cradle. The sea has been Punic a long time.

units.name: Heptereme of the Suffetes
units.description: A towering seven that serves as flagship, floating fortress, and statement of policy. Few enemies fight it; most simply give way.

units.name: Nile Spear Levies
units.description: Fellahin called up between flood and harvest, spears in hands more used to sickles. The river gives Egypt more of them than any rival can bury.

units.name: Desert Axemen
units.description: Frontier soldiers with the bronze khopesh and heavy axe, garrisoning the desert roads. Heat, thirst, and raiders have already culled the weak ones.

units.name: River Guard
units.description: The standing regiments of the river cities, drilled in the tight new fashion the dynasts brought from over the sea. Old land, new spears.

units.name: Nile Bowmen
units.description: Archery is Egypt's oldest trade after farming, and these levies practice both. Their massed volleys have opened battles for two thousand years.

units.name: Pharaoh's Bowmen
units.description: Picked archers of the royal establishment bearing composite bows of horn and sinew. At two hundred paces they choose which eye.

units.name: Delta Horsemen
units.description: Light riders from the delta estates, better at scouting the wadis than breaking a line. Egypt's strength was never in the saddle.

units.name: Pharaoh's Chariots
units.description: Gilded cars in the ancient style, each bearing a driver and a master archer of the royal school. Antique, splendid, and still lethal on open ground.

units.name: Axemen of Horus
units.description: Temple soldiers marked with the falcon god's eye, wielding great bronze axes blessed at the sanctuary. They fight as men already promised to the sky.

units.name: Companions of the Palace
units.description: Armored riders of the court who shadow the general as the god's living standard. While one still breathes, so does his lord.

units.name: Delta War Galley
units.description: A broad-beamed galley built of imported cedar, as at home in the river mouths as on the open sea. It carries archers enough to sting before it rams.

units.name: Tribal Warband
units.description: Every free man of the tribe with spear, long shield, and something to prove. Their first charge can break a line; their second rarely comes.

units.name: Tribal Skirmishers
units.description: Landless youths who fight from the treeline with fistfuls of light javelins. Killing one is easy; finding one is the trick.

units.name: Forest Hunters
units.description: Bowmen who feed their families from the deep woods and feed the crows in war. They shoot from cover, and the forest is all cover to them.

units.name: Tribal Light Horse
units.description: Riders on shaggy ponies who raid at dawn and are legend by dusk. They fight for plunder, which keeps them wonderfully motivated.

units.name: Gallic Long Swords
units.description: Warriors of standing with the long slashing blade the smiths of Gaul are famous for. They come on singing, and the song is about you.

units.name: Gallic Oathsworn
units.description: Champions bound by oath to a chieftain's table, wearing the torcs of men who have never run. Each has a name-song; none intends it to end badly.

units.name: Gallic Noble Riders
units.description: Chieftains' sons in mail their fathers paid for in cattle and iron. The best horsemen north of the Alps, and they will tell you so.

units.name: Germanic Spear Wall
units.description: Clansmen locked shield to shield in a wall their fathers taught them to build. It moves slowly, gives ground never.

units.name: Berserkers
units.description: Men who go to battle bare-chested and god-mad, biting their shield rims until the fury takes them. They cannot be frightened, only killed, and killing them is slow.

units.name: Woad Raiders
units.description: Island warriors painted in blue spirals that mark them as already claimed by their gods. They burst from the mists howling, which is usually enough.

units.name: British War Chariots
units.description: Light wicker cars that deliver a champion to the fight and snatch him out again, drivers running the yoke-pole at full gallop for show. Horses that have never seen one bolt outright.

units.name: Falx Reapers
units.description: Highlanders swinging the great two-handed falx that opens helmets like shellfish. They trade their own safety for wounds no surgeon will attempt.

units.name: Falcata Warriors
units.description: Peninsular fighters with the forward-curved blade that bites like an axe and cuts like a sword. They strike from ambush, vanish, and strike again.

units.name: Numidian Desert Riders
units.description: Bridleless riders guiding their mounts with a stick and a word, casting javelins and melting away. No cavalry on earth catches them; most stop trying.

units.name: Numidian Javelineers
units.description: Herdsmen who learn the javelin defending goats from lions and jackals. Armies, they find, are slower than either.

units.name: Numidian Spear Levies
units.description: Villagers of the high plains with hide shields and light spears. They are not the kingdom's pride, but they hold a hilltop while the riders work.

units.name: Camel Scouts
units.description: Riders on groaning desert beasts that cross sands no horse survives. The camels' reek alone throws enemy cavalry into confusion.

units.name: Scythian Horse Archers
units.description: Grass-sea nomads who ride before they walk and shoot before they speak. Their retreat is a weapon; their pursuit is a sentence.

units.name: Scythian Noble Archers
units.description: Chieftains' kin in scale shirts sewn from horse-hoof and bronze, as ready with the sword as the bow. Gold-hilted, grave-bound, and glorious.

units.name: Scythian Foot Archers
units.description: Camp followers and the horse-poor, still deadly with the short recurved bow every wagon carries. Even a Scythian without a horse is a Scythian with a bow.

units.name: Steppe Spear Levies
units.description: Settled tributaries of the horde, armed with pike-length spears to guard the wagon laagers. The steppe hardens even its farmers.

units.name: Warlord's Companions
units.description: Sworn companions who feast at the warlord's fire and die at his shoulder. To come home without him is to have no home.

units.name: Raiding Longboats
units.description: Hide-sailed, shallow-drafted boats that slip up estuaries no war galley dares. Built for raiding, they fight at sea only when cornered.

units.name: Cretan Archers
units.description: Islanders whose bows have decided other people's wars for generations. Expensive, professional, and worth every drachma they overcharge.

units.name: Balearic Slingers
units.description: Islanders raised with a sling in each fist and fed, as boys, only what they could knock off a post. Their lead shot cracks helmets at absurd range.

units.name: Gallic Sword-Hands
units.description: Exiles and younger sons selling the long blade to whoever pays in gold or glory. They fight like men with nothing to lose, which is precisely what they are.

units.name: Hired Hoplites
units.description: Veterans of the endless Greek wars, spear and shield for rent by the season. Their loyalty runs exactly as deep as the pay chest.

units.name: Hired War Elephants
units.description: Beasts and mahouts hired as a matched set from the southern trade towns. Ruinously costly, occasionally ruinous to their employer, always ruinous to someone.

units.name: Numidian Hire-Riders
units.description: Desert horsemen who follow the wars north for silver and remounts. Ask them to skirmish forever; never ask them to hold a line.

units.name: Boarding Marines
units.description: Legionaries drilled to cross the raven's bridge with the deck heaving under them. Fighting on land they keep the habit: close fast, grip hard, and give no ground that took blood to win.
